method: Each row was transcribed by reading its question crop (questionImage, a path in the source repository; questionImageSha256 is the crop registry hash). Wording, part labels and mark brackets follow the printed question; maths uses linear notation; diagrams get a short bracketed description of what is printed, never the answer. Page furniture (page numbers, barcodes, 'Question N is on the back page.') is omitted.
reason: The delivered accessibleText was PDF text extraction: flattened maths (for example 'y x x 2 3 2 = - -' for y = |x^2 - 2x - 3|) and barcode control characters (U+0001 to U+0008). QuestionExplorer serves accessibleText as the screen-reader transcript.

supersedes.note: The app serves these transcriptions in place of the delivered accessibleText. The source repository file is unchanged and still hash-pinned; every other field of every delivered row is served verbatim.

conventions: Powers: x^2, e^(x-2), 8^(2x+1); inverse functions g^-1(x); units km h^-1, cm^2.
Fractions: a/b, with brackets around compound parts: (x^2 - 8)/(3 - x), 1/(2x).
Minus is the ASCII hyphen-minus; spaces around top-level operators, none inside exponent brackets.
Symbols as in the bank's well-formed maths rows: √, ≤, ≥, °, π, θ, ×, ∫; modulus |...|; log_5 x for a logarithm to base 5.
Column vectors are written (top, bottom) and noted as column vectors; a vector RS is written 'vector RS'.
Diagrams: [Diagram: ...] at the position they are printed.

rows.accessibleText: 1 A polynomial p is given by p(x) = 4x^3 + 8x^2 - x - 2. (a) Show that x + 2 is a factor of p(x). [1] (b) Solve the equation p(x) = 0. [3]

2 (a) On the axes, sketch the graph of y = |x^2 - 2x - 3|. State the intercepts with the coordinate axes. [4] [Diagram: blank axes for the sketch, with the x-axis horizontal, the y-axis vertical and the origin O.] (b) The function g is defined by g(x) = 4e^(x-2) - 1 for all real x. Find an expression for g^-1(x). [2]

3 In this question, time t is in seconds and displacement s is in metres. A particle starts from rest at the origin O and moves in a straight line with constant positive acceleration. When t = 4, s = 6. (a) Draw the velocity-time graph for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. [2] [Diagram: a grid with velocity on the vertical axis, marked 0, 2, 4 and 6, and time on the horizontal axis, marked 0, 2 and 4.] (b) Hence find the acceleration. [1]
4 In an arithmetic progression: • the common difference is -2 • the sum of the first 4 terms is equal to the sum of the first 10 terms. Find the first term. [3]
5 A curve has equation y = (x^2 - 8)/(3 - x). P and Q are the stationary points on the curve. Find dy/dx and the exact length of the line PQ. [7]
6 (a) Solve the equation |3x + 2| = 7. [3] (b) Solve the inequality |2x - 4| > |x + 1|. [4]
7 The variables x and y are related by y = 3√x + 1/√x. Use calculus to find the approximate change in y when x increases from 4 to 4 + h, where h is small. [4]

8 A curve has equation y = xe^(2x+1). (a) Find dy/dx. [3] (b) The line L is the tangent to the curve at the point where x = 1/2. Find the exact coordinates of the two points where L meets the axes. [5] (c) Use your answer to 8(a) to find ∫ xe^(2x+1) dx. [4]

9 (a) In this question, time is in seconds and distances are in metres. At time t = 0, particle A starts at the origin and moves with velocity (2, 1). At the same time, particle B starts from the point with position vector (-3, 4) and moves with velocity (4, -2). [The vectors are printed as column vectors.] (i) Write down the position vector of B at time t. [1] (ii) Determine whether or not the particles collide. [4] (b) The point Q has position vector 3i + 2j. The point R has position vector -i + 4j. The point S has position vector ai + bj, where a and b are integers. It is given that: • S lies on the straight line QR • |vector RS| = √5. Find the possible values of a and b. [5]
10 (a) Given that log_5(x^2) - log_5 x - 3 log_x 5 = 2, find x. [6] (b) Solve the equation 2 × 8^(2x+1) - 3 × 2^(3x+4) - 64 = 0. [4]
11 A curve has equation y = -x^2 + 3ax - 2a^2 where a is a positive constant. The area of the region enclosed by the curve and the x-axis is 9/16. Find the value of a. [6]
12 Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the circles with equations x^2 + 2x + y^2 - 4y - 20 = 0 and x^2 - 12x + y^2 - 6y + 20 = 0. [8]

1 The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 4 for all real values of x. (a) Write f(x) in the form a(x + b)^2 + c where a, b and c are constants. [3] (b) Hence find the range of f. [1] (c) The function g is defined by g(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 4 for x ≤ k, where k is a constant. Given that g has an inverse, state the largest possible value of k. [1] (d) The function h is defined by h(x) = e^(3x) - 1 for x ≤ 0. Given that gh(x) exists, find gh(x), simplifying your answer. [3]

2 Points A and B have coordinates (1, 3) and (-7, 1). The point P with coordinates (2, a) lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB. (a) Find the value of a. [4] (b) The point Q is the reflection of P in the line AB. Find the coordinates of Q. [2]

3 [Diagram: a grid with x marked from -4 to 4 and y marked from -6 to 8, showing the cubic curve, which crosses the x-axis at x = -2, x = 1 and x = 3 and the y-axis at y = 6.] The diagram shows the graph of y = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3). By drawing a suitable line on the diagram, solve the inequality (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3) > 7. [4]

4 (a) A 6-digit number is to be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. No digit may be used more than once in any 6-digit number. Find how many 6-digit numbers can be formed in the following cases. (i) There are no further restrictions. [1] (ii) The 6-digit number includes the digit 4. [2] (b) A class contains 10 girls and 12 boys. A group of 6 students is to be selected from the class. There must be at least 2 girls and at least 2 boys in the group. Find the number of different selections that can be made. [3]

5 The diagram shows a design for a badge. [Diagram: triangle ABC, with C at the top, drawn with dashed sides; each side is replaced by a circular arc bulging outwards, and the width from A to B is labelled x cm.] ABC is an equilateral triangle with side x cm. The arcs BC, CA and AB are parts of the circles with centres A, B and C respectively. (a) Write down the size of angle ABC in radians. Give your answer in terms of π. [1] (b) The area of the badge is 2(π - √3) cm^2. Find x. [5]

6 (a) The diagram shows part of the graph of y = 1 + tan((1/2)x) where x is measured in degrees. [Diagram: a grid with no scale marked, showing repeating branches of the curve separated by dashed vertical asymptotes; the asymptote labelled A is the second one to the right of the y-axis.] (i) Write down the period of 1 + tan((1/2)x). [1] (ii) Write down the equation of the asymptote A. [1] (b) On the axes below, sketch the graph of y = 3 cos 2x + 1 for -180° ≤ x ≤ 180°. [3] [Diagram: a blank grid with x marked at -180°, -90°, 0, 90° and 180°, and y marked from -6 to 6.]

7 A ship is sailing with speed v km h^-1. The sailing cost per hour, $C, is given by C = v^2 + 3000/v + 100. (a) Find the speed that makes C a minimum. Justify that this value of C is a minimum. [5] (b) Hence find the minimum sailing cost for a journey of 150 km. [3]
8 A circle has centre (-2, 0) and radius 5. A line has equation y = 2x + k, where k is a constant. The line does not meet the circle. Find the set of possible values of k. [8]

9 (a) Show that tan θ + cot θ + 2 sec θ can be written as (1 + 2 sin θ)/(sin θ cos θ). [3] (b) Hence solve the equation tan 2x + cot 2x + 2 sec 2x = 0 for -180° ≤ x ≤ 180°. [4] (c) Solve the equation 3 sec(x - 1) - 1 = tan^2(x - 1) where x is in radians and -1 < x < 3. [5]

10 In this question time t is in seconds and displacement s is in metres. For t ≥ 0, a particle moves on the positive x-axis. At time t the acceleration of the particle is 2t - 9. At time t = 7 the velocity of the particle is 4. (a) Find the times when the velocity of the particle is 0. [4] (b) At time t = 12, the displacement of the particle from the origin O is 150. (i) Find an expression for the displacement of the particle at time t. [3] (ii) Find the distance travelled by the particle in the first 6 seconds. [3]

11 (a) Find, in descending powers of x, the first three terms in the expansion of (x^2 + 1/(2x))^9. Give each term in its simplest form. [3] (b) The expansion of (x^2 + 1/(2x))^n, where n is a positive integer, has a term that is independent of x. Show that n is divisible by 3. [4]
